 Jeremiah Fears, Dejounte Murray, Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey and Karlo Matković will start Monday’s game against the Warriors. 
 The Pelicans are without Trey Murphy and Zion Williamson for Monday’s game, leaving two spots open in the starting lineup. Jones and Bey will fill the voids, with the latter being the better streamer for fantasy managers seeking offensive production. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Zion Williamson (rest) is out for Monday’s game against the Warriors. 
 The Pelicans will be without two of their top four scorers on Monday, as Williamson has joined Trey Murphy (knee) on the shelf. Saddiq Bey’s role will take on added importance, whether he moves into the starting lineup or not. 
 Trey Murphy 
 NOP 
 Forward 
 #25 
 Trey Murphy III (knee) is questionable for Monday’s matchup with the Warriors. 
 Murphy III is a late addition to Monday’s injury report, which doesn’t bode well for his availability against Golden State. If Murphy III is ultimately sidelined, Saddiq Bey and Herbert Jones could absorb his minutes. 
 Trey Murphy 
 NOP 
 Forward 
 #25 
 Trey Murphy (knee) finished Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 10 points (3-of-7 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer. 
 Back in the Pelicans’ lineup after sitting out Wednesday’s win over the Jazz, Murphy played 34 minutes against the Timberwolves. While he did record four of his five assists in the second half, the Pelicans’ forward also attempted just one shot. Given Murphy’s importance to the team offensively, that can’t happen. Murphy’s return pushed Herb Jones (zero points, four rebounds), who had a frustrating night and fouled out in 14 minutes. 
 Saddiq Bey 
 NOP 
 Forward 
 #41 
 Saddiq Bey accounted for 17 points (5-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 At first glance, Bey’s 17 points might suggest a good night overall. However, he scored 12 of those points in the fourth quarter, shooting 3-of-4 from the field and 3-of-3 from the foul line. Bey didn’t provide much value in the first three quarters, which hurt the overall field-goal percentage. The fourth quarter allowed those rostering Bey to salvage some value, and he remains a player who should be rostered in some 12-team leagues.

 Murphy was given a probable designation on Thursday afternoon, so this latest update isn’t a surprise. Expect Murphy to steal some playing time from Herb Jones and Saddiq Bey.

 NOP 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dejounte Murray (personal) will start Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Given Jeremiah Fears’ play while Murray was away for personal reasons, some questioned whether the veteran point guard would start on Wednesday. Murray will, with Trey Murphy’s knee tendinitis making things easier for Pelicans head coach Jamahl Mosley. This also means that Herb Jones will remain in the starting lineup.

 #25 
 Trey Murphy (knee) has been downgraded to questionable to play against the Jazz on Wednesday. 
 While there is still a chance Murphy plays, trending down is never a good sign. If he doesn’t suit up, there is a decent chance Herb Jones remains a starter, even with Dejounte Murray returning. Saddiq Bey would also be in line for extra minutes. 
 Dejounte Murray 
 NOP 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Dejounte Murray (personal) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Murray has missed the Pelicans’ last three games for personal reasons, and Herb Jones has replaced him in the starting lineup. Jeremiah Fears has played well as the sole point guard in Murray’s absence, which could force Pelicans head coach Jamahl Mosley to make a tough decision on Wednesday.

 Cooper Flagg authored a dominant performance to lead the Mavericks to a 125-122 win over the Pacers on Monday, delivering a season-high 43 points (16-of-25 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, six assists, three steals and one block over 38 minutes.
 Unreal. Flagg delivered 16 clutch points in the fourth quarter alone, joining veteran teammate Kyrie Irving to account for 78 of Dallas’ 125 points in an impressive victory. The 19-year-old prodigy has now scored at least 20 points in seven of his first 10 games, delivering first-round fantasy value while averaging an elite 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists, 2.2 steals and 0.8 blocks per contest. It’s difficult to imagine a more impressive start to the season for a player still in his teens.
 -  George Bissell

 Kyrie Irving matched a season-high with 35 points (11-of-18 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs) and four assists over 38 minutes in Monday’s win over the Pacers.
 It was a two-man show for Dallas in this one with Irving and Cooper Flagg combining for an eye-popping 78 of their 125 points. The pair hoisted 43 shot attempts total and connected on 10-of-16 three-pointers. Seven of those conversions from long range came courtesy of Irving as he put together one of his best shooting efforts in recent memory, matching his previous season-high mark in the scoring department set against the Rockets back on October 30. The 34-year-old point guard is putting together an impressive campaign, averaging 22.9 points, 3.2 rebounds, 4.3 assists and 1.2 steals through nine games.

 Jabari Smith Jr. accounted for 14 points (6-of-13 FGs), seven rebounds, three assists and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
 After a quiet first half, Smith shot 4-of-6 from the field in the second half, scoring 10 points. Since scoring 52 points in the Rockets’ final two games of October, he’s cooled off offensively.  Alperen Şengün finished Monday’s win over the Nuggets with 20 points (9-of-17 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.
 Like Kevin Durant, Şengün finished Monday’s victory two assists shy of a triple-double. The Rockets center held his own against three-time NBA MVP Nikola Jokić, playing efficient basketball as both a scorer and a playmaker. Şengün is closing in on first-round value in 12-team leagues, a few spots ahead of his preseason ADP (18). While some may consider selling high, they should also consider that this may be who Şengün is at this point in his career and hold onto him.

 Kevin Durant recorded 23 points (6-of-15 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), 12 rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
 Remember the concerns about Durant’s lack of shot attempts after Houston’s November 2 win over the Celtics? He’s attempted at least 14 shots in each of the Rockets’ last three games, scoring at least 21 shots in each appearance. Durant’s field-goal percentage against the Nuggets wasn’t the best, but he finished two assists shy of a triple-double in what was a productive night overall.

 Ty Jerome went off for 27 points (9-of-19 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), six rebounds and two assists over 32 minutes to propel the Grizzlies to a 118-102 win over the Raptors on Monday.
 Jerome has been an absolute scoring machine for Memphis, delivering at least 20 points in seven of nine contests this season. The 29-year-old point guard matched a season-high by knocking down five three-pointers while supplying his usual diet of driving layups and off-balance mid-range floaters. He’s significantly outperformed preseason expectations, delivering second-round fantasy value so far, averaging 26.7 points through his first nine games. He’s shown zero signs of slowing down and should continue to serve as the Grizzlies’ main offensive weapon.
